text:
emma: FYI — after the OFED/firmware push last night in eu-west-2 we've got multiple training jobs reporting 2-4x slower allreduce. seeing consistent bandwidth drop across p4d pods :rotating_light:
raj: confirmed on our side. nccl throughput graphs show a cliff at the same rollout timestamp, cross-az traffic looks fine until huge retrans counts.
olga: I ran a quick job repro on a small 8x config, baseline 44GB/s, now ~11-13GB/s. tcp fallback observed in NCCL logs: 
micah: can you paste the nccl logs snippet?
emma: here's the important bits:
```
NCCL WARN Unhandled transport/Connect error: rdma_connect: Connection timed out
NCCL INFO Falling back to PCIe/TCP for ring 2
```
raj: also seeing kernel messages on hosts: 
```
[ 1234.567890] efa0: subchannel trimmed, peer 10.0.2.5, qp state ERR
[ 1234.568012] mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: MLX5_AE: port 1 down, link recover in progress
```
olga: ibv_devinfo shows the devices present but ib stats show a spike in retransmits and rcv errors.
micah: did the OFED package include the new mlx5 driver or only userland? deployment notes said kernel module update + firmware roll for IB cards.
emma: it included a firmware bump on mlx5 and the ofed 6.0 stack. we rolled this to all eu-west-2 hosts in batches 00:30–02:10 UTC.
luke: quick question — is this cross-az only or intra-az as well?
raj: mostly cross-az flows (az-a <-> az-c) showed the worst degen, intra-az less severe but still measurable. suggests path MTU or routing fallback interplay.
carla: customers on Dedicated in eu-west-2 are alerted?
emma: infra-oncall-bot created INC-2026-341 and sent a notice to status.redwood.ai (ops alert).
infra-oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-341 created: "eu-west-2 NCCL bandwidth regression after low-level network stack update" — pager sent.
micah: repro steps I ran: small allreduce (nccl-tests) between 8 GPUs, before patch: 42GB/s, after patch: 12GB/s. run command: 
```bash
mpirun -np 8 ./all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 4096 -f 2 -g 1
```
and check dmesg on both ends.
raj: potential root causes we should consider: firmware bug on mlx5 causing packet coalescing/regression; OFED 6 user/kernel mismatch; MLX5 driver ABI/feature change altering XDP/TSO offloads; MTU negotiation issue causing fragmentation.
olga: quick mitigation options:
- rollback firmware + driver to previous known-good baseline (risky; requires reboot)
- force NCCL to prefer IB (set NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0? actually the inverse — force RDMA transport?)
- reduce MTU to 1500 temporarily on IB interfaces to avoid fragmentation
- enable a per-cluster TCP fallback tuning for capacity-sensitive jobs

luke: rollback seems safest for immediate restoration but will need reboots and a maintenance window. how many hosts affected?
emma: ~120 hosts in eu-west-2 (all GPU nodes). we can do a partial rollback on a subset (50%) to validate.
raj: cost/impact: rolling back halves our pool for a short time unless we reschedule jobs. some Dedicated customers have reserved capacity — we must coordinate with accounts.
carla: I'll loop in account-ops for customer comms if we go for rollback. heads up: two enterprise customers have latency-sensitive jobs running now.
micah: technical note — before rebooting we can try toggling mlx5 params on one host: 
```bash
# try disabling tso/gso on mlx5 netdev as a quick test
ip link set dev eth0 tx off rx off
ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off sg off
```
if that restores throughput, it's likely offload interaction.
raj: good idea. emma, can you run that on one degraded host and run nccl test?
emma: doing that now on host euw2-gpu-045. will post numbers. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
(emma updates after ~10m)
emma: after disabling offloads throughput improved to ~36GB/s on that host pair. that strongly implicates offload/driver interaction.
olga: nice find. so firmware/driver/offload combo is the culprit.
micah: that means rollback of driver/firmware or a blacklist change is required. blacklist will be quicker but fragile.
luke: what's the risk of leaving offloads disabled cluster-wide? CPU overhead will go up, but for short-term it's acceptable if perf restored.
raj: estimate CPU penalty ~10-15% on data path for heavy allreduce jobs. acceptable for a 24–48h mitigation while we plan rollback.
carla: I recommend we: (1) implement offload disable via a daemonset on all GPU nodes in eu-west-2 for emergency mitigation, (2) schedule phased rollback of firmware+driver next week with reboots, (3) notify customers and open a support RFO.
emma: I'll create a daemonset patch and roll to 100% in 30m after testing on canary hosts.
micah: also file a bug with vendor (Mellanox) with kernel logs + dmesg + repro. include that disabling offloads is a workaround.
raj: agree. action items: 
- emma: deploy daemonset to disable offloads (canary -> 50% -> 100%) [ETA 1h]
- micah: vendor bug + gather logs [ETA 2h]
- carla: customer comms + incident updates [ETA 30m]
- olga: schedule rollback plan if vendor can't confirm fix [ETA EOD]

emma: starting canary now. posting canary results when done.
carla: adding ops:oncall and accounts on the incident.
infra-oncall-bot: Update INC-2026-341: mitigation in progress — offload disable daemonset rolling to canary (1/5).
luke: add a note to postmortems channel once stabilized — include exact kernel/firmware versions and marchback plan.
emma: canary looks good: canary pair bandwidth back to ~40GB/s. rolling to 50% next.
raj: ok prioritize ASM jobs restart policy so they pick recovered nodes first.
micah: will follow up with a root cause writeup once vendor replies. also add perf dashboards to detect offload-induced cliffs automatically.
carla: thanks all. will keep customers posted. :thumbsup:
